svg.text: FIG 01: TRANSIENT PHYSICAL FOUNDATIONS, ENERGY CONTINUITY & BOUNDARY STATE MODELS
Energy Storage Axioms • Mechanical Inertia Analogy • Finite Power Barrier • The 3 Canonical Temporal Boundary Regimes (t = 0⁻, 0⁺, ∞)

g.text: The Physical Origin: Stored Field Energy
• Transients represent the time-dependent transitional response of voltages
and currents between two equilibrium steady states following a switching event.
Root Cause: Memory elements store energy in electromagnetic fields:
Electrical networks map directly to classical Newtonian mechanical systems:
• Just as physical mass cannot jump velocity instantaneously without infinite force,
inductor current cannot jump instantaneously without infinite voltage!
• Purely resistive networks contain NO memory elements (zero L, zero C).
• Stored energy is identically zero at all times: E(t) ≡ 0 J.
• When switch operates, voltages and currents step INSTANTANEOUSLY between
the two DC levels without any exponential settling curve.
Governed by pure algebraic Ohm's law: v(t) = i(t) · R.
Transients exist IF AND ONLY IF at least one dynamic storage element (L or C) is present!
(Or during electromagnetic wave propagation along distributed transmission lines).
In any linear time-invariant dynamic network, complete response x(t) decomposes
naturally along two dual mathematical perspectives:
• x_natural(t): Complementary Function (CF), decays to 0 as t → ∞ (Transient).
• x_forced(t): Particular Integral (PI), driven by independent source (Steady State).
• Zero-Input Response (ZIR): Response due SOLELY to initial stored energy
(i_L(0⁻), v_C(0⁻)) with all independent external sources set to zero.
• Zero-State Response (ZSR): Response due SOLELY to external input excitation
x_ZIR ≠ x_natural in general! ZIR contains natural terms, but ZSR contains
BOTH forced steady-state AND transient natural components!
Why cannot capacitor voltage or inductor current jump discontinuously?
Power is the rate of energy transfer: P(t) = dE/dt.
Suppose stored energy changes by a finite step ΔE ≠ 0 in time Δt → 0:
• Practical sources (batteries, generators) possess FINITE voltage and FINITE current.
• Infinite power is physically impossible in ordinary circuits.
Therefore, stored energy MUST BE A CONTINUOUS FUNCTION OF TIME!
The State Continuity Invariants at t = 0
Under all finite excitations (steps, ramps, sinusoids):
• v_L(t) = L · di_L/dt. If i_L stepped discontinuously, di/dt = δ(t) ⟹ v_L → ∞!
• i_C(t) = C · dv_C/dt. If v_C stepped discontinuously, dv/dt = δ(t) ⟹ i_C → ∞!
Finite terminal voltages and currents GUARANTEE state continuity!
DANGER: Only i_L and v_C are guaranteed to be continuous!
The following quantities CAN AND DO JUMP discontinuously at t = 0⁺:
1. Inductor Voltage: v_L(0⁺) CAN JUMP! v_L(0⁺) ≠ v_L(0⁻) in general.
2. Capacitor Current: i_C(0⁺) CAN JUMP! i_C(0⁺) ≠ i_C(0⁻) in general.
3. Resistor Voltages: v_R(0⁺) CAN JUMP! (Resistor has zero memory).
4. Resistor Currents: i_R(0⁺) CAN JUMP! (Follows algebraic KVL/KCL).
5. State Derivatives: di_L/dt(0⁺) and dv_C/dt(0⁺) CAN JUMP!
Exam Rule: Never assume v_L(0⁺) = v_L(0⁻) or i_C(0⁺) = i_C(0⁻)!
• Infinitesimal instant immediately BEFORE the switch moves.
• Circuit is in prior DC steady state. All transients from past events have settled.
• Mathematical point of topological discontinuity. Switch opens or closes.
• Infinitesimal instant immediately AFTER the switch establishes new topology.
Dynamic elements carry their frozen continuity states: i_L(0⁺)=i_L(0⁻), v_C(0⁺)=v_C(0⁻).
Duality Note: L and C swap behaviors between initial instant and steady state!
State 1: Evaluating Initial Conditions at t = 0⁻
If circuit has been connected to DC sources for a very long time before t = 0:
• All transients have decayed to zero; time derivatives vanish: d/dt ≡ 0.
Inductor: v_L = L · di/dt = L · 0 = 0 V ⟹ SHORT CIRCUIT
Capacitor: i_C = C · dv/dt = C · 0 = 0 A ⟹ OPEN CIRCUIT
1. Draw equivalent circuit at t = 0⁻ with all L shorted and all C opened.
2. Solve purely resistive DC circuit for inductor currents i_L(0⁻) and capacitor
voltages v_C(0⁻) with correct signs and arrow orientations!
State 2: The Instantaneous Model at t = 0⁺
Immediately after switch changes state, dynamic elements act as DC sources:
Replace with an Independent Current Source of value I₀ = i_L(0⁻).
(Arrow oriented in the original current direction; if i_L(0⁻) = 0, acts as OPEN circuit!).
Replace with an Independent Voltage Source of value V₀ = v_C(0⁻).
(Polarity matching v_C(0⁻); if v_C(0⁻) = 0, acts as SHORT circuit!).
At t = 0⁺, the entire dynamic circuit becomes PURELY RESISTIVE with DC sources!
State 3: The Final DC Steady State at t = ∞
After new switch configuration has remained unchanged for t ≫ 5τ:
• All transient currents and voltages have fully extinguished.
• Inductor once again becomes a SHORT CIRCUIT (v_L(∞) = 0 V).
• Capacitor once again becomes an OPEN CIRCUIT (i_C(∞) = 0 A).
1. Draw equivalent circuit under the NEW switch topology at t = ∞.
2. Replace L with short circuit and C with open circuit.
3. Solve standard DC network for final target values x(∞) = i_L(∞) or v_C(∞).
With x(0⁺) and x(∞) known, solution is 66% complete in 60 seconds!
The switching boundary instants correspond to extreme frequency limits in s-domain:
1. High-Frequency Limit: s → ∞ ⟺ Initial Instant t → 0⁺
Z_L(s) = s · L ⟶ ∞ Ω (Inductor behaves as OPEN CIRCUIT)
Z_C(s) = 1 / (s · C) ⟶ 0 Ω (Capacitor behaves as SHORT CIRCUIT)
(Valid for initially uncharged elements with zero initial stored energy!).
2. Low-Frequency / DC Limit: s → 0 ⟺ Final Steady-State t → ∞
Z_L(s) = s · L ⟶ 0 Ω (Inductor behaves as SHORT CIRCUIT)
Z_C(s) = 1 / (s · C) ⟶ ∞ Ω (Capacitor behaves as OPEN CIRCUIT)
Initial & Final Value Theorems in s-Domain
Extracting boundary states directly from the Laplace transform X(s):
FVT is valid IF AND ONLY IF all poles of [s · X(s)] lie strictly in the open
LEFT HALF of the s-plane! (If poles exist on jω axis, e.g. LC tanks, FVT FAILS!).
De-energize dynamic derivatives; solve prior DC resistive circuit for i_L(0⁻) and v_C(0⁻).
Apply continuity: i_L(0⁺)=i_L(0⁻), v_C(0⁺)=v_C(0⁻). Replace L with I₀ source, C with V₀ source.
Under final switch topology, set L → short, C → open. Solve new DC resistive circuit.
Mastering these 3 boundary states solves 80% of all GATE transient questions!
